description: System definition for the edge type vocabulary. Declares the discipline of using a small canonical edge palette.

content.purpose: Edges connect nodes. The Enki knowledge graph uses a small, stable set of edge types so traversal queries are predictable and so the graph stays legible to humans and machines alike.
content.principle: A small palette of well-defined edges is more powerful than many ad-hoc ones. If a relationship doesn't fit, refine an existing type or add via ceremony — never invent inline.
content.directionality: Edges are directed. Each edge has a source and target. Some edge types have inverse counterparts (cites/cited_by, supersedes/superseded_by). The edge writer is responsible for creating both sides where applicable.
content.evidence: Each edge carries an evidence string and a strength (0.0–1.0). Edges created by AI extraction also carry an ai_generated flag. Human-confirmed edges override AI ones via supersedes.
